heroHeadline: Trump Pushes Lebanon Truce to Save Iran MoU — Publicly Constrains Israeli Beirut Advance; Reuters: Iran Preparing to Decline US Proposal; Lebanon Toll 3,468+; Hormuz 94-Day Paralysis — Day 95
heroSubtitle: Day 95 (June 2, 2026): Trump told ABC News an Iran Hormuz/ceasefire deal is reachable 'within the next week,' claiming to have personally secured commitments from Netanyahu and Hezbollah intermediaries to pause Beirut strikes. In a reportedly heated phone call, Trump pressed Netanyahu to scale back Israel's Lebanon ground offensive and publicly declared Israeli forces would not advance on Beirut — the most direct public US-Israel constraint since Day 82. Lebanese authorities confirmed Hezbollah agreed to a US proposal under which strikes on Beirut would cease. Round 4 US-hosted Lebanon-Israel talks convened at the State Department, led by Deputy NSA Mike Needham and Ambassador Mike Huckabee with Israeli and Lebanese ambassadors. Despite Trump's push, Reuters reported Iran was preparing to formally decline the current US MoU proposal; Ghalibaf warned a permanent halt to negotiations if Israel's Lebanon campaign continues. The Lebanese Health Ministry reported the toll reached 3,468+ killed — a sharp rise from 3,162+ reported just one day earlier. Northern Israeli schools were permitted to reopen, suggesting some de-escalation along the border. CNN Business reported 94 days of Hormuz paralysis: only 7 ships transited the prior Friday; 39 vessel strikes and 11 maritime deaths since Feb 28; a cargo vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the northern Persian Gulf. Analysts warned disruption is expected to last through 2026 absent a deal.
